record.question: What are you thinking of?
options: What has been thought of by you?
What is thought of by you?
What is being thought of by you?
What was thought of by you?
record.explanation: The active question uses present continuous are thinking of. The corresponding passive uses is being thought of, retains the preposition of, and expresses the agent as by you. The resulting question is formal and awkward but grammatical, and it alone preserves the source tense and aspect. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/free-resources/grammar/english-grammar-reference/active-passive-voice
